title: Curators must prove authorization while Guardians must justify discretion, and their reporting duties differ accordingly
content:
The two reporting requirements look parallel and are not. A.6.1.1.1.3.9.3.3 requires a Curator to post within 24 hours "a transaction hash of the action, the UTC time at which the timelock period for the action elapses, a description of the action being implemented, and **a link to the poll which provided governance approval** for the action." A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.3.2 requires a Guardian to post "a transaction hash of the action, a description of the action, **general reasoning for the action, and justification for the action being within the governance-approved mandate**."

The difference tracks the difference in the underlying authority. A Curator never exercises judgment — its legitimacy is entirely derivative, so its report is a *citation*: here is the poll, here is the transaction, compare them. No reasoning is requested because none should exist.

A Guardian, by contrast, cancels in real time on one of four enumerated grounds, with no prior vote to point at. Its legitimacy is a claim about the situation, so its report must argue: why it acted, and why the act fell inside a mandate nobody voted on specifically. The Guardian's report is the only record of a decision that was made unilaterally.

This is the correct asymmetry for any system that pairs a mechanical executor with a discretionary circuit breaker. Demanding reasoning from the Curator would invite exactly the discretion the framework removes; accepting a bare citation from the Guardian would leave its most consequential power unexplained.

Both deadlines are 24 hours from submission — which for the Curator lands well inside the minimum three-day timelock. The report arrives while the action can still be cancelled, making it an input to the oversight window rather than a record of a completed act.
description: Both report within 24 hours, but the Curator supplies a link to the approving poll and timelock expiry while the Guardian supplies reasoning and a justification that the act was within mandate.
